questions.stem: A 26-year-old man comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. He was diagnosed with HIV infection 2 weeks ago. His CD4+ T-lymphocyte count is 162/mm3. An interferon-gamma release assay is negative. Prophylactic treatment against which of the following pathogens is most appropriate at this time?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pneumocystis jirovecii

Pneumocystis jiroveci :Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP) is a lung infection caused by a fungus. It's rare in healthy people, and usually affects those with a weak immune system.



Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number:862.

questions.stem: A Patient on antimicrobial therapy develops the following signs and symptoms that ultimately are found to be drug-induced (Cough, dyspnea, pulmonary Infiltrates, neutropenia, and bleeding tendencies). Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient’s symptoms?
questions.solutionHtml:
Nitrofurantoin

Nitrofurantoin is an antibiotic that fights bacteria. It is used to treat and prevent uncomplicated urinary tract infections. It works by killing the bacteria that cause such diseases. But, it will not treat a viral infection.



Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 810
